> Hey guys, a little update for request type, is missing the URL parameter:
> 
> request: { agentOptions: { keepAlive: true, family: 4 }, url: "https://api.telegram.org", }

I think this is unnecessary since node-telegram-bot-api already fills that parameter with the correct URL, unless you're doing something really customized for your use-case you shouldn't do that.

I am facing the same error with nodejs v20 and ubuntu 22.04 on virtual machine (VM). but there is no error on my local computer with nodejs v20 and macos. I downgraded the nodejs version to v14 on VM and it worked fine.

### **I have a potential cause and interim work around**
**Cause**
Home network has no IPv6 connection but Raspi has IPv6 enabled, even a IPv6 address (command ip a will show).
**Solution**
DIsable IPv6 on Raspi (for example by [https://fleetstack.io/blog/disable-ipv6-raspberry-pi#:~:text=How%20to%20Disable%20IPv6%20on%20Your%20Raspberry%20Pi,Reboot%20Your%20Raspberry%20Pi%20...%206%20Conclusion%20] ) and node-red-contrib-telegrambot now works with Node 20.
**Underlying cause (maybe)**
I would hypothesis that node20 changed preferred IP and how it determines if ipv6 is available, rather than checking a live IPv6 connection, it takes the existence of a IPv6 address as IPv6 exists.

I have proved this fix with the node-red-contrib-telegrambot node (issue 343) that uses this node.

I also experienced this on Ubuntu VPS, initially my project used PM2 and it had an error, but after I tried running it without PM2 it was normal, so I moved it from PM2 to Screen so that the bot was always active.
Might be bug in newer NodeJs - workaround here https://github.com/yagop/node-telegram-bot-api/issues/1193#issuecomment-2639099713

I kept getting **EFATAL AggregateError**, so I went to investigate.
Turns out that if you pass following arguments:
```
const bot = new telegramAPI(config.botToken, { polling: true, request: {
    agentOptions: {
        keepAlive: true,
        family: 4
    }
}});
```
In my case, the error changed to:
```
Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 149.154.167.220:443
```
Which I found odd. Sure enough, that IP was _completely unreachable_ for me, even using ping or per browser. 
My first thought was: Have I been IP banned for whatever reason? After all, the IP _does ping_ using a VPN or over 4G on my phone!

After some thinking, I logged into my router, and sure enough, I had region blocking on and one of the countries banned was "United Kingdom", which coincidentally happens to be where the CDN is located, even though I'm **nowhere near**.
Removed it from the deny list, and voilá, **it started working**!

**So, in other words, if you're pulling your hair out, check first if the firewall isn't blocking the IP or connection! Could be your antivirus, your router, or both.**
